sections.heading: Bottoms-up initiative
sections.content: The example is a developer spotting something wrong and going off to fix it. Yuhki says that when people across the company are constantly trying to make the product better, he generally tries not to get in their way; these fixes can improve the quality of the experience more effectively than a top-down effort to define a quality metric and change things, which might miss specific problems. He also says that when an engineer or designer is trying to fix a real, customer problem, his response is “by all means.”
